summary: The customer wants to know what parameters to clarify and what initial comparison experiment to perform before selecting a fiber-based optical spectroscopy system to monitor water in a petroleum process stream from an analyzer located outside the process area.

facts_stated.text: The process handles a petroleum stream.
Current testing involves sending samples to an off-line laboratory for water analysis.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: currently send samples to a laboratory for water determination

facts_stated.text: The analyzer unit is intended to be positioned outside the process area.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: The analyzer would be outside the process area.

targets.purpose: detect process changes more quickly than off-line laboratory analysis

process.enquiry_quote: currently send samples to a laboratory for water determination

process.value: Closer to the process than the current laboratory
Fast enough that changes are detected sooner
process.enquiry_quote: so that changes can be noticed sooner

process.value: Analyzer located outside the process area connected via fiber
process.enquiry_quote: The analyzer would be outside the process area.

unknowns: Expected water concentration range (trace ppm dissolved vs. percent level free/emulsified water)
Exact hydrocarbon matrix composition and optical properties (color, transparency, scattering, or high NIR/MIR background absorption)
Physical state of water in the stream (fully dissolved, emulsion, or stratified phases)
Process temperature, line pressure, and flow rates at the intended probe installation point
Physical distance between the measurement point and the analyzer location outside the process area
Hazardous area (Ex/ATEX) classification at the probe location and along the fiber run
Current laboratory reference method (e.g., Karl Fischer titration) and required precision/detection limits
Potential probe fouling mechanisms (asphaltenes, waxes, scale, particulate matter) and cleaning/maintenance constraints
